fixes.explanation: Twelve is a long stretch already, friend. But Moses gives a bigger number for the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered. He says 38 years (Deuteronomy 2:14). That's more than three times what you picked, and it ends only when that whole generation of fighting men has perished from the camp.

Seven years would be a long trip, I'll give you that. Moses puts it much higher for the road from Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Zered: 38 years (Deuteronomy 2:14). Seven doesn't even get you halfway, friend.

Carmel never shows up in this passage. Moses says that for many days they wandered around Mount Seir (Deuteronomy 2:1). It's like texting the wrong Mike when you've got three Mikes in your contacts. The name feels right in the moment, but Seir is the mountain this verse names.

That's the reason the LORD gives. He says, “…because I have given Mount Seir to Esau as his possession.” So none of that land is going to Israel, “…not even a footprint…” Not one footprint's worth! When God hands something to somebody, friend, it's theirs. I've had folks eye my cookie dough like that, and it's still mine.

Yes! The note says Esau's people drove out the Horites and settled in their place, “…just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.” Think about that, friend. Israel is walking past Esau's family right now, and Moses reminds them that Esau's people settled their land the same way Israel settled theirs. Both lands came with the LORD's hand in it. I love a little side note that quietly says, 'You're not the only ones, baker.'

True! When they get close to the Ammonites, the LORD says, “…do not harass them or provoke them…” And He gives His reason: “…for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites.” Notice the pattern, friend. That's Edom, then Moab, and now Ammon. Three neighbors, and each time the LORD says the land is already given. Israel's whole job is to walk by and keep their hands to themselves.
